Subject: [Show-off / Valuation] 1994 Portuguese Time Capsule: Master System II Super Pack 3 + Buggy Run
Posted: Thu Nov 12, 2026 7:51 pm (GMT 0)

Hello everyone! I wanted to share my childhood Sega Master System II set, bought in Portugal back in 1994 and kept in storage since then.
Since SMS Power is the ultimate resource for regional variants, I thought you might appreciate seeing a complete Portuguese Ecofilme (the official local distributor) time capsule:
• Console: Master System II (Super Pack 3) in great cosmetic shape, original unbroken seals/screws, tested and working perfectly. Includes the original cardboard insert (1994 late run), 1 controller, and the original RF switch box still with its factory protective plastic film and unused adhesive tape on the back.
• Paperwork: Original 1994 store receipt, stamped warranty card, fold-out Sega Games Catalog poster, Epilepsy warning leaflet, handwritten password sheet from the 90s, and the rare Portuguese "Clube SEGA" registration card.
• Games (All CIB with yellow Ecofilme seals): World Games, Klax, Pac-Mania, and the crown jewel: Buggy Run CIB.
• Buggy Run details: Complete with manual, 100% intact plastic hangtab, and the long white Ecofilme Portuguese translation sticker on the back of the case.
I would love to hear the community's thoughts on this Portuguese variant and what you estimate its current market value to be! Feel free to send a PM if you have any questions.
I can send you photos if you want.

entry.title: Development :: RE: [WIP] Tactical-RPG for the MS by cireza
entry.dc:creator: cireza
entry.dc:subject: Development
entry.content:
Author: cireza
Posted: Thu Nov 12, 2026 1:58 pm (GMT 0)

badcomputer wrote
What's the reason for locking background and sprite palettes to the same 16? I'm not that familiar with this type of game but I thought only the background tiles flash when selecting etc?


You have two types of tiles to display at once : those where you can walk, and those were you cannot. So what you do is that you put the walk tiles on a palette and the non-walk tiles on the other palette.

And then you make the palette effect you wish on the walk tiles : make them brighter, make them blink. Or you could even decide to make all the non-walk tiles darker. I experimented all of these actually.

So basically, both palettes are a copy of each other, with one having the "walk effect" you have decided applied on it.

Then comes the issue of not having a separate background layer : you have to merge the units over the BG tiles because you cannot use sprites (you can align units on the entire screen which doesn't fit of course).

So you end up using these 16 colors for both units and BG.

Now let's say you want the ground to blink, but not the units. How do you achieve this ? Well you don't really have the choice : you are forced to separate the palette in 2. You use one half for the ground, and the other for the characters. And you only apply your "walk effect" on the colors used by the ground. This leads to pretty simplistic visuals, and this is what Shining Force did on Game Gear.

In my case, I decided not to divide the palette, so when I make a tile brighter, it applies to both the ground AND the unit. So I only put the current moving unit on the clear palette, and all others remain on the normal palette. The fact that I am drawing at a higher scale than SF on GG requires more gradients to look good too.

At first I had decided to not use a palette effect for the walk area. I was actually using a second set of tiles that all had a small dot displayed on them. Example here :


They were forged with a mask so they didn't use ROM space.

It works, but this wastes a lot of VRAM though since I have to duplicate all tiles. This means I have to give up on having both lower and uppercase letters on the map, and also reduces the number of unique tiles from 128 to 96 to build the map.

However, this frees one palette entirely. Ultimately, I found that using a palette effect was more in line with the capabilities of the console and helped improve the presentation.

entry.content:
Author: bbayles
Posted: Thu Nov 12, 2026 12:46 pm (GMT 0)

I just wrote up a new cheat for The Adventures of Batman & Robin:

  • During gameplay, press Press Right, Left, Right, Left, Right, Left, Right.
  • Hold 1 and press Start. Coordinate will appear onscreen.
  • Hold 1 and press the D-pad to move Batman through walls and floors
  • Hold 1+Start and press Left/Right to change the stage number. Press 2 to warp to the selected stage.


There were previously Action Replay codes to enable these features, but I think the button sequence method is new!

I also figured out part of what's going on with the mysterious "FUCKS CRACKS SONY1" strings in the game data. They're special passcodes! You have to enter them as "FTCKS CQACK SNNY1", since the game alters the second character before checking. They don't do much, however - each one takes you to a different level, but nothing beyond that. Strange!
